A cheque is a bank order that directs the bank to pay the person the stated sum of money. The stated amount is deducted from the drawer’s (account) and transferred to the beneficiary’s account or given in cash. This is one of the most important banking instruments that people have used for a long time. Cheques are a good way to carry a significant amount of money without being noticed. Banks issue chequebooks on the account holder’s request. However, there are several types of cheques and not every account holder is eligible for all types of cheques. Some accounts such as fixed deposits or recurring accounts do not usually require a bank account unless these are combined with a savings account. The banks hold this authority and they can suspend the cheque facility of any account holder at any time. Types of Cheques: Indian banking system has two types of basic bank accounts, viz. savings account and current bank account. In Both the accounts, the account holders are provided with different types of chequebooks. However, how a cheque functions largely depends on the way of issuing a cheque. A cheque issued for savings account can function differently as per the will and mode of signing of the drawer (issuer). Here are a few common ways that show the different types of issued cheques. Bearer’s Cheque: Cheque leaves printed with the word ‘bearer’ are called bearer cheques. This indicated that the person holding the cheque is eligible for the stated amount. The banks dispense the stated amount to the person holding the cheque. Bearer’s cheques are most vulnerable to frauds. A misplaced bearer’s cheque can cause you severe financial loss as anyone can encash the cheque from the bank. Self Cheque: Self cheques can be issued for withdrawing money from your own bank account or given to a third party as well. A cheque becomes a self cheque when you write your name on it. You can also write ‘self’ and give the cheque to a third party. However, writing self on cheques is not safe as anyone can claim the cheque and withdraw the funds. Pay Yourself Cheque: These cheques are issued for buying bank drafts, pay orders and fixed deposits receipts. Pay yourself cheques are issued with a crossing on them as the drawer wants the bank to deduct the money from his/her bank account. PDC (Post Dated Cheque): Post dated cheques are given for encashing at a specific time. The bearer cannot encash the cheque before the stated time in any condition. These cheques are handy for making EMI payments. Crossed Cheque: A cheque crossed with two parallel lines on the top left corner is an account payee cheque that transfers the funds directly into the beneficiary’s account. The name of the beneficiary is written on the cheque and it cannot be negotiated for a cash withdrawal. These cheques are relatively safer than any other for making payments and transferring funds. Order Cheque: Despite not having any marks, an order cheque is only payable to specific company or person. You

The payment may be subject to verification of required and submitted documents. If the depositor fails to submit the required documents then the bank may hold the release of the payment. Time Demand Draft The demand draft is paid by the bank only after a specific period of time has passed which is the demand draft clearing time. Time demand draft has an expiry date after which the bank shall not release the payment. Moreover, the payment is made after a certain time has passed. Limitations of a Demand Draft A Demand Draft represents a transaction that has already taken place. Hence, it cannot be cancelled once it is delivered to the payee. If the demand draft gets lost, stolen, or altered with and the funds are cashed out by the wrong person, the bank is not responsible for replacing the lost money. Demand draft is valid only for 3 months and if not encashed in this time frame, the payee is at a loss of funds. Demand Draft Cancellation A demand draft cancellation letter is written to withdraw the raised demand draft for the transaction. There could be several reasons to cancel the demand draft. If an individual wants to cancel the raised demand draft, he/she will have to write a DD cancellation application to the bank where the individual has applied it and submit it to the bank. Note: If you have paid in cash at the time of issuing your demand draft, you will be able to retrieve payment in cash only. However, if the payment is made through cheque, the amount will be credited to your bank account. what is account transfer fees (PPF Account Deposit slip)

Expected Answer

An account transfer fee is a transaction charge applied when moving money or financial assets between accounts, generally categorized into electronic funds transfers or institutional brokerage migrations. In India, web-based digital routing methods such as UPI, NEFT, and RTGS are entirely free for retail savings customers when executed via mobile apps or online net banking portals. If you choose to visit a physical bank branch to execute an NEFT or RTGS transaction manually, small slab-based service fees ranging from ₹2 to ₹50 (plus applicable GST) will be charged. On the other hand, sending money across international borders triggers much higher costs, including outward wire transfer fees, third-party correspondent bank deductions, and foreign currency conversion markups.

These guidelines should be brought to the notice of all customers apart from being disclosed on the bank's website. 5.5 Purchase of Local Cheques, Drafts, etc., during suspension of Clearing There may be occasions when Clearing House operations may have to be temporarily suspended for reasons beyond the control of the authorities concerned. Such suspension entails hardship to the constituents of the banks because of their inability to - 14 - DBR-Master Circular on Customer Service in Banks 2015 realize promptly the proceeds of cheques, drafts, etc., drawn on the local banks other than those with whom they maintain accounts. Some remedial action has to be taken during such contingencies to minimise, as far as possible, the inconvenience and hardship to banks' constituents as also to maintain good customer service. Thus, whenever clearing is suspended and it is apprehended that the suspension may be prolonged, banks may temporarily accommodate their constituents, both borrowers and depositors, to the extent possible by purchasing the local cheques, drafts, etc., deposited in their accounts for collection, special consideration being shown in respect of cheques drawn by Government departments/companies of good standing and repute, as also demand drafts drawn on local banks. While extending this facility, banks would no doubt take into consideration such factors as creditworthiness, integrity, past dealings and occupation of the constituents, so as to guard themselves against any possibility of such instruments being dishonoured subsequently. 5.6 Statement of accounts / Pass Books 5.6.1 Issuance of Passbooks to Savings Bank Account holders (Individuals) (i) A passbook is a ready reckoner of transactions and is handy and compact and as such, is far more convenient to the small customer than a statement of account. Use of statements has some inherent difficulties viz., (a) these need to be filed regularly (b) the opening balance needs to be tallied with closing balance of last statement (c) loss of statements in postal transit is not uncommon and obtaining duplicates thereof involves expense and inconvenience (d) ATM slips during the interregnum between two statements does not provide a satisfactory solution as full record of transactions is not available and (e) there are a large number of small customers who do not have access to computers / internet, etc. As such, non-issuance of pass-books to such small customers would indirectly lead to their financial exclusion. Banks are therefore advised to invariably offer pass book facility to all its savings bank account holders (individuals) and in case the bank offers the facility of sending statement of account and the customer chooses to get statement of account, the banks must issue monthly statement of accounts. The cost of providing such Pass Book or Statements should not be charged to the customer. - 15 - DBR-Master Circular on Customer Service in Banks 2015 (ii)

An initial account deposit can be made in hard cash for any total valuation up to rupees one lakh. The accepted modes of deposit for a PPF Account using the deposit slip include:

1. **Cash Deposit**: You can deposit cash at the bank counter using the PPF deposit slip.
2. **Cheque Deposit**: You can also deposit a cheque made out for the PPF account.

The deposit slip needs to be filled out with your account details, and once submitted, you will receive a stamped acknowledgment.

What Is a Deposit Slip? A deposit slip is a standard form provided by banks that you fill out when depositing cash or a cheque at a bank branch. It serves as a written record of the transaction for branch processing and gives the depositor an acknowledgement of what was submitted. When you hand over the filled slip along with cash or a cheque, the bank usually keeps one copy of the original and stamps the customer portion before returning it to you. This stamped copy is an important record of submission and can help if there is a delay, a mismatch, or a dispute about the deposit. Banks maintain records of deposit transactions for operational, audit, and compliance purposes. A deposit slip or stamped acknowledgement is one of the basic documents used to support that record-keeping. In everyday banking, deposit slips are still widely used for branch-based cash deposits, cheque deposits, third-party deposits in permitted cases, and business cash handling. Even with digital banking becoming more common, this simple form continues to matter because it helps link the money or cheque being submitted to the correct account. Deposit Slip vs. Pay-In Slip - Are They the Same? Yes, in India, "deposit slip" and "pay-in slip" are generally used interchangeably. Both refer to the form used to deposit money into a bank account at a branch. In common usage, they mean the same thing. That said, the exact naming can vary by bank, branch, and form layout. Some banks may use the term "cash deposit slip," others may say "pay-in slip," and some may use labels like "cash/cheque deposit voucher." The difference is usually about terminology, not function. Term Common Usage Deposit Slip Often used in private sector banking and general consumer language Pay-In Slip Common in public sector bank branches and traditional banking usage Cash/Cheque Deposit Voucher Used by some banks and institutions for specific branch formats From a practical user’s point of view, both terms usually refer to the same type of branch deposit form. Types of Deposit Slips in India Not all deposit slips are identical. The type of form depends on what you are depositing and how the bank handles that transaction. what denominations can i use to deposit (PPF Account Deposit slip)

When filling out a cash deposit slip, you can list your currency notes under the standard active denominations of ₹500, ₹100, ₹50, ₹20, and ₹10. Generated Answer

When depositing into a Public Provident Fund (PPF) account using a deposit slip, you can typically use Indian currency denominations such as ₹2, ₹5, ₹10, ₹20, ₹50, ₹100, ₹200, ₹500, and ₹2000 notes. However, it is advisable to check with your specific branch for any restrictions or preferences regarding denomination breakdown, especially since the PPF deposit slip includes a denomination table for cash deposits. Keep in mind that the minimum deposit is ₹500 and is subject to a maximum of ₹1,50,000 per annum.

What Is a Deposit Slip? A deposit slip is a standard form provided by banks that you fill out when depositing cash or a cheque at a bank branch. It serves as a written record of the transaction for branch processing and gives the depositor an acknowledgement of what was submitted. When you hand over the filled slip along with cash or a cheque, the bank usually keeps one copy of the original and stamps the customer portion before returning it to you. This stamped copy is an important record of submission and can help if there is a delay, a mismatch, or a dispute about the deposit. Banks maintain records of deposit transactions for operational, audit, and compliance purposes. A deposit slip or stamped acknowledgement is one of the basic documents used to support that record-keeping. In everyday banking, deposit slips are still widely used for branch-based cash deposits, cheque deposits, third-party deposits in permitted cases, and business cash handling. Even with digital banking becoming more common, this simple form continues to matter because it helps link the money or cheque being submitted to the correct account. Deposit Slip vs. Pay-In Slip - Are They the Same? Yes, in India, "deposit slip" and "pay-in slip" are generally used interchangeably. Both refer to the form used to deposit money into a bank account at a branch. In common usage, they mean the same thing. That said, the exact naming can vary by bank, branch, and form layout. Some banks may use the term "cash deposit slip," others may say "pay-in slip," and some may use labels like "cash/cheque deposit voucher." The difference is usually about terminology, not function. Term Common Usage Deposit Slip Often used in private sector banking and general consumer language Pay-In Slip Common in public sector bank branches and traditional banking usage Cash/Cheque Deposit Voucher Used by some banks and institutions for specific branch formats From a practical user’s point of view, both terms usually refer to the same type of branch deposit form. Types of Deposit Slips in India Not all deposit slips are identical. The type of form depends on what you are depositing and how the bank handles that transaction. No. A deposit slip is generally used to deposit cash or cheques into a bank account. A challan is typically a prescribed form for statutory or government payments. How to Fill a Deposit Slip - Step-by-Step Filling a Cash Deposit Slip Filling a cash deposit slip correctly is simple, but small mistakes can create delays or even result in the bank refusing to accept the slip. Step 1: Write the date Enter the date in the format required on the form, usually DD/MM/YYYY. Step 2: Enter the account number carefully Write the full account number exactly as it appears in your passbook, cheque book, or banking app. One wrong digit can send the money to the wrong account or cause the deposit to be held. Step 3: Write the account holder’s name Use the name as per bank records. Writing clearly helps the teller verify the deposit quickly. Step 4: Add your mobile number If the slip asks for a mobile number, enter the correct one. This can help if the bank needs to contact you regarding the transaction. Step 5: Fill the denomination table Count the notes properly and mention the number of notes against each denomination. Example: ₹500 × 10 = ₹5,000 ₹100 × 5 = ₹500 Total = ₹5,500 Step 6: Write the total amount in figures Enter the exact total in numeric form. Step 7: Write the amount in words Write the same amount in words to avoid mismatch. Step 8: Provide PAN details where applicable PAN is generally required when cash deposits exceed ₹50,000 in a single day with a banking company or co-operative bank. If PAN is not available, Form 60 may be required in eligible cases. Step 9: Sign the slip Sign in the depositor’s signature field. If you are depositing into someone else’s account, you sign as the depositor. Step 10: Submit the slip and cash Hand over the filled slip and the cash to the teller. Step 11: Collect the stamped customer copy Keep this copy until the deposit is properly reflected in your bank account. It is an important acknowledgment of submission. Filling a Cheque Deposit Slip Cheque deposit slips are slightly different because you are depositing an instrument rather than physical cash. Step 1: Fill date, account number, and account holder name These basic details should be entered clearly. Step 2: Leave the denomination section blank This section applies to cash, not cheques. Step 3: Enter cheque details Mention: cheque number cheque date issuing bank name branch name, if required cheque amount Step 4: Write the amount in figures and words If the form asks for both, make sure they match. Step 5: Follow branch instructions on cheque endorsement Some banks ask customers to write the account number and sign on the back of the cheque. However, this is not a universal rule in exactly the same format across all banks, so follow the printed branch or bank instruction.

Question
--------
what other details should I keep in mind to have to fill in the form (PPF Account Deposit slip)

Expected Answer
---------------
Your account number , Cheque / Demand Draft  No & Date , Bank / Branch on Which Drawn

Generated Answer
----------------
When filling out the Public Provident Fund (PPF) account deposit slip, here are the key details to keep in mind:

1. **Date**: Enter the current date (usually in DD/MM/YYYY format).

2. **Account Number**: Make sure to write the full PPF account number correctly, as any error could lead to deposit complications.

3. **Account Holder Name**: Use the name as registered with the bank.

4. **Deposit Amount (Figures)**: Enter the amount you are depositing in numeric form. This helps to avoid confusion.

5. **Deposit Amount (Words)**: Write the same amount in words. This is important for verification and to prevent any discrepancies.

6. **Denomination Table**: If you are depositing cash, break down the cash into various denominations (like ₹500 notes, ₹100 notes, etc.) and clearly indicate the number of each denomination.

7. **PAN/Form 60**: If your deposit exceeds ₹50,000 in cash in a single transaction, you must provide your Permanent Account Number (PAN) or Form 60, as applicable.

8. **Signature**: Ensure you sign the slip. If you are depositing into someone else’s account, use your signature in the depositor’s signature field.

9. **Additional Information (if needed)**: Some banks may require additional information about the purpose of the deposit or the relationship with the account holder, especially for third-party deposits.

10. **Collect a Receipt**: After submitting the slip, make sure to collect a stamped copy or receipt as it serves as proof of your deposit.

Make sure to review the slip for any omissions or errors before submission to ensure a smooth transaction.

Question
--------
what happens if i deposit more than the acceptable ammount (PPF Account Deposit slip)

Expected Answer
---------------
The moment a branch office identifies that a customer's total account balance has crossed the legally prescribed maximum investment ceiling, it must take immediate action. The bank is required to formally contact the depositor in writing, officially instructing them to remove the surplus funds from the account without delay.

Generated Answer
----------------
If you deposit more than the maximum allowable amount of Rs. 1,50,000 in a Public Provident Fund (PPF) account during a financial year, the excess amount will not earn any interest and will not be eligible for tax rebate under the Income Tax Act. Therefore, it is important to ensure that your total annual deposits do not exceed the specified limit to not inadvertently lose out on interest earnings or tax benefits.

QUESTION 171
======================================================================

Question
--------
what details of mine are needed to add nominee (Public Provident Fund Account Nomination Form)

Expected Answer
---------------
Name of the account holder , the account number and addressand data

Generated Answer
----------------
To add a nominee to your Public Provident Fund (PPF) account, you typically need to provide the following details in the Public Provident Fund Account Nomination Form:

1. **Name of the Nominee**: The full name of the person you wish to nominate.

2. **Relationship with the Nominee**: You need to specify your relationship to the nominee (e.g., spouse, child, parent, etc.).

3. **Date of Birth of the Nominee**: If the nominee is a minor, you will need to provide their date of birth.

4. **Address of the Nominee**: The complete residential address of the nominee.

5. **Share of Nominee**: If you are nominating more than one person, you can indicate the share of each nominee.

6. **Your Signature**: You will need to sign the nomination form to authorize the nomination.

It's advisable to check with your bank or the specific form guidelines for any additional required information or documentation.

(FAQ) Public Provident Fund 1. What is a PPF Account? It is a Government of India Scheme. PPF account is opened under the Public Provident Fund Scheme,1968. PPF Scheme,1968 introduced vide GSR 1136(E), dated 15.06.1968 and was rescinded vide GSR 913 (E) dated 12.12.2019. PPF Scheme 2019 was reintroduced vide GSR 915 (E) dated 12.12.2019. It is savings- cum -tax saver scheme for Indian residents only. 2. Who can open an account under PPF? Any resident individual can open account for himself/herself and on behalf of a Minor or a person of unsound mind as a Guardian. 3. What are the documents required for opening a Public Provident Fund (PPF) account with SBI? PPF account opening form (Form 1) Nomination Form Passport size photograph Copy of PAN Card/ Form 60-61 Copy of Aadhaar / Aadhaar Enrolment Number 4. Is Aadhaar required to open PPF Account? Yes, PPF account can be opened with Aadhaar as primary identity. If Aadhaar number has not been assigned to the customer, proof of Aadhaar enrolment number can be provided to open the account. However, customer has to submit Aadhaar within six months from account opening date for linking. If Aadhaar has not been submitted within six months from account opening date, account shall cease to be operational till the time the customer submits the Aadhaar. 5. Is PAN / Form-60 required to open PPF Account? Yes, PPF account can be opened with PAN/Form-60. If customer has not submitted PAN at the time of account opening, PAN has to be submitted within a period of two months from the date of happening of any of the following events, whichever is earliest, The balance at any point of time in the account exceeds Rupees fifty thousand, or The aggregate of all credits in the account in any financial year exceeds Rupees one lakh, or The aggregate of all withdrawals and transfers in a month from the account exceed Rupees Ten thousand. In the event of failure of submitting PAN within the specified period of 2 months, the account shall cease to be operational till the time the customer submits the PAN. 6. What is the maximum age limit for opening a PPF account? There is no maximum limit of age for a person to open a PPF account. A person of any age can open an account. 7. Can a person with unsound mind open a PPF account? Yes, individuals as Parents/ Guardians on behalf of a person with unsound mind can open PPF account. 8. What are the documents required to open a PPF account of a person with unsound mind? For opening such an account, Guardian needs to submit a certificate from Superintendent of Mental Hospital where a person of unsound mind is confined or treated, along with PPF account opening form (Form 1), Nomination Form, Passport size photograph, Copy of PAN card/ Form 60-61, and Aadhaar as Identity proof and Residence proof as per Bank's KYC norms. 9. QUESTION 172

Question
--------
what details of the nominees are needed (Public Provident Fund Account Nomination Form)

Expected Answer
---------------
names of nominees , address of nominees , date of birth in case of minor else age and proportionate amount

Generated Answer
----------------
To complete the Public Provident Fund (PPF) Account Nomination Form, the following details of the nominees are typically required:

1. **Name of the Nominee**: The full name of the person(s) being nominated.
2. **Relationship with the Account Holder**: The nature of the relationship between the account holder and each nominee (e.g., son, daughter, spouse, etc.).
3. **Age of the Nominee**: The age of each nominee, particularly if the nominee is a minor.
4. **Nominee’s Address**: The residential address of each nominee for identification purposes.
5. **Proportion of Shares**: If there are multiple nominees, the account holder can specify the share or proportion of the account amount that each nominee will receive.

These details help ensure that the correct individuals are designated as nominees and can facilitate the distribution of funds upon the account holder's demise.

# (FAQ) Public Provident Fund 1. What is a PPF Account? It is a Government of India Scheme. PPF account is opened under the Public Provident Fund Scheme,1968. PPF Scheme,1968 introduced vide GSR 1136(E), dated 15.06.1968 and was rescinded vide GSR 913 (E) dated 12.12.2019. PPF Scheme 2019 was reintroduced vide GSR 915 (E) dated 12.12.2019. It is savings-cum-tax saver scheme for Indian residents only. 2. Who can open an account under PPF? Any resident individual can open account for himself/herself and on behalf of a Minor or a person of unsound mind as a Guardian. 3. What are the documents required for opening a Public Provident Fund (PPF) account with SBI? - PPF account opening form (Form 1) - Nomination Form - Passport size photograph - Copy of PAN Card/ Form 60-61 - Copy of Aadhaar / Aadhaar Enrolment Number 4. Is Aadhaar required to open PPF Account? Yes, PPF account can be opened with Aadhaar as primary identity. If Aadhaar number has not been assigned to the customer, proof of Aadhaar enrolment number can be provided to open the account. However, customer has to submit Aadhaar within six months from account opening date for linking. If Aadhaar has not been submitted within six months from account opening date, account shall cease to be operational till the time the customer submits the Aadhaar. 5. Is PAN / Form-60 required to open PPF Account? Yes, PPF account can be opened with PAN/Form-60. If customer has not submitted PAN at the time of account opening, PAN has to be submitted within a period of two months from the date of happening of any of the following events, whichever is earliest, - The balance at any point of time in the account exceeds Rupees fifty thousand, or - The aggregate of all credits in the account in any financial year exceeds Rupees one lakh, or - The aggregate of all withdrawals and transfers in a month from the account exceed Rupees Ten thousand. In the event of failure of submitting PAN within the specified period of 2 months, the account shall cease to be operational till the time the customer submits the PAN. 6. What is the maximum age limit for opening a PPF account? There is no maximum limit of age for a person to open a PPF account. A person of any age can open an account. 7. Can a person with unsound mind open a PPF account? Yes, individuals as Parents/ Guardians on behalf of a person with unsound mind can open PPF account. 8. What are the documents required to open a PPF account of a person with unsound mind? For opening such an account, Guardian needs to submit a certificate from Superintendent of Mental Hospital where a person of unsound mind is confined or treated, along with PPF account opening form (Form 1), Nomination Form, Passport size photograph, Copy of PAN card/ Form 60-61, and Aadhaar as Identity proof and Residence proof as per Bank's KYC norms. 9. QUESTION 173
======================================================================

Question
--------
what happens in case of adding minors in nominees (Public Provident Fund Account Nomination Form)

Expected Answer
---------------
A adult has to sign teh form to whom the amount will be trasfered to incase of death of the account owner or maturing of the account

Generated Answer
----------------
In the Public Provident Fund (PPF) account nomination process, if a minor is named as a nominee, the following key points apply:

1. **Guardian Requirement**: Since a minor cannot manage their own affairs, the legal guardian will need to operate the account on behalf of the minor nominee until the minor reaches the age of majority.

2. **Payment to Guardian**: In case of the account holder's death, the balance in the PPF account will not be paid directly to the minor. Instead, it will be managed by the guardian until the minor reaches maturity. Once the minor attains majority, they will be able to claim the balance in the account directly.

3. **Multiple Nominees**: The account holder can nominate one or more individuals, including minors, as nominees. The account holder can also specify the share allocated to each nominee, including minors.

4. **Operational Continuity**: The account remains operative, and the funds can be managed according to the rules that govern the PPF scheme until the nominated minor attains majority. The guardian can continue to manage the account until then.

5. **Legal Requirements**: The nomination form must indicate that the nominee is a minor, and the name of the guardian responsible for managing the nominee's share must be clearly mentioned.

It is essential to comply with all regulatory requirements and to provide relevant documents that confirm the guardian's relationship to the minor nominee when necessary.

(9) State of PPF account in the event of death of the guardian of the minor or the death of the minor:- The matter has been examined in consultation with the Ministry of Law and the following clarifications are issued. 20 Point raised i In the event of death of guardian, in relation to a minor, whether PPF account standing in the name of the minor should be closed and a new account opened Clarification In the case of an account opened on behalf of a minor, the minor is treated as subscriber. The amount in the account of a minor does not become payable on the death of the guardian, because, under Section 8 of the PPF Act the amount becomes payable only on the death of the subscriber. In case of death of guardian the account of minor remains operative and a new account need not be opened. The surviving natural guardian or a guardian appointed by competent court may continue the account of minor after producing necessary guardianship certificate. ii In the event of death of the minor subscriber whether the balance in the account is payable to the guardian. In the event of death of the minor subscriber the guardian does not ifsofacto becomes entitled to the payment of the balance. The balance in such cases is payable to the legal heirs of the minor in accordance with Section 8 of PPF Act and para 12(6) of the Public Provident Fund Scheme. It will continue till the death of its last member or the HUF is dissolved. When the Karta passes away, the PPF HUF account does not expire. It is handled by the new Karta, the senior member of the HUF. If the senior member is not in a position to work as Karta, some other member can work as Karta. The ITO will be informed and his approval taken. After taking approval of the ITO, the Accounts Office will be informed by the new Karta through an application supported with a copy of the approval letter of the ITO, death certificate of the deceased Karta and revised application form for opening the account duly signed by the new Karta. The new Karta will continue the account till it is matured. If a nominee was appointed by the deceased Karta, the nominee who will be one of the members of the HUF, will become the new Karta and he will continue the account. QUESTION 177
======================================================================

Question
--------
what can the nominees do incase of death of the depositor (Public Provident Fund Account Nomination Form)

Expected Answer
---------------
If a subscriber to an account in respect of which a nomination is in force dies, the nominee or nominees may make an application in Form G or, as near thereto as possible, to the Accounts Office together with proof of death of the subscriber and on receipt of such application all amounts standing to the credit of the subscriber after making adjustment, if any, in respect of interest on loans taken by the subscriber shall be repaid by the Accounts Office itself to the nominee or nominees.

Generated Answer
----------------
In the event of the death of the depositor of a Public Provident Fund (PPF) account, the nominees have the following rights and responsibilities:

1. **Application for Payment**: The nominee(s) can make an application in Form G, or a similar format, to the Accounts Office along with proof of the death of the subscriber. 

2. **Claiming Amount**: Upon receipt of the application, the Accounts Office will repay all amounts standing to the credit of the deceased subscriber after any necessary adjustments related to interest on loans taken by the subscriber.

3. **Survivorship**: If there are multiple nominees and one of them has passed away, the surviving nominee(s) must also provide proof of the deceased nominee's death along with their claim.

4. **Closure of Account**: The nominee is required to close the account by withdrawing the full amount due in one installment. Part payments in more than one installment are not allowed.

5. **Interest Accrual**: The balance in the PPF account continues to earn interest until the end of the month preceding the month in which the payment is made.

6. **Limit on Payment Without Legal Certificate**: If there is no nomination in force at the time of the subscriber's death, the nominees (or legal heirs) may still claim the amount after fulfilling certain documentation requirements, including indemnity letters and affidavits, provided that amounts do not exceed specified limits.

These provisions ensure that the nominees are facilitated in collecting the amounts due under the account in a structured manner.

(5) A Public Provident Fund account on behalf on a minor can be opened by
---
A Public Provident Fund (PPF) account can be opened by resident Indian Individuals and individuals on behalf of Minors or a person of unsound mind. Only one Public Provident Fund (PPF) account can be maintained by an Individual, except an account that is opened on behalf of a Minor / a person of unsound mind. A Public Provident Fund (PPF) account can be opened either by the Mother or Father on behalf of their Minor Son or Daughter. However, the Mother and Father both cannot open Public Provident Fund (PPF) accounts on behalf of the same Minor.

QUESTION 178
======================================================================

Question
--------
what happens incase no nominees are mentioned (Public Provident Fund Account Nomination Form)

Expected Answer
---------------
The amount after the substraction of any fees will be transfered to the legal heirs of the account owener

Generated Answer
----------------
If no nominees are mentioned at the time of opening a Public Provident Fund (PPF) account, the amount standing to the credit of the deceased subscriber will be payable to the legal heirs upon the subscriber's death. In this case, the amount will be divided among the legal heirs based on the applicable laws of succession. The process would typically involve the legal heirs submitting an application in Form G, along with proof of death and other required documents. Additionally, for balances up to ₹1 lakh, payment may be made to the legal heirs without needing to produce a succession certificate, but they must submit certain affidavits and indemnity letters as specified in the regulations.

QUESTION 179
======================================================================

Question
--------
what about the interest to be paid by the nominees after death of the account owner (Public Provident Fund Account Nomination Form)

Expected Answer
---------------
The nominee/heir to the deceased subscriber is liable to pay interest on loans availed of by the subscriber but not paid before his death.

Generated Answer
----------------
The nominees or heirs to the deceased subscriber of a Public Provident Fund (PPF) account are liable to pay interest on any loans that the subscriber availed of but had not repaid before their death. This means that if there were outstanding loans against the PPF account at the time of the subscriber's death, the nominee or legal heir would be responsible for settling that interest.

It's important to note that the nominee themselves does not become the owner of the account or its funds. They are designated to collect the funds on behalf of the legal heirs, and payment to the nominee does not affect the legal rights of the heirs under succession laws.

Question
--------
can I extend my PPF account as a NRI (Public Provident Fund Account Extension Form-)

Expected Answer
---------------
An amendment was made to Rule 3 of PPF Scheme 1968 vide MOF Notification No. GSR 585 (E) dated 25.7.2003; Non Resident Indians are not eligible to extend/continue PPF account after maturity. It has been clarified by the Ministry of Finance that accounts opened under such category cannot continue beyond maturity; therefore any subscription made by the depositor is irregular and not entitled for interest. Amount deposited after maturity, shall be refunded to the account holder without interest.

Generated Answer
----------------
No, you cannot extend your Public Provident Fund (PPF) account if you are an NRI (Non-Resident Indian). While a resident who becomes an NRI during the maturity period may continue to subscribe to the fund until its maturity on a non-repatriation basis, those accounts cannot be extended further.

Question
--------
can a person holding power of attorney extend the PPF account (Public Provident Fund Account Extension Form-)

Expected Answer
---------------
no the person holding power of attorney cannot operate or hold the ppf account

Generated Answer
----------------
No, a person holding a Power of Attorney cannot extend a Public Provident Fund (PPF) account. The guidelines specify that a Power of Attorney holder can neither open a PPF account nor operate any PPF account on behalf of a subscriber, as there is no provision in the PPF Scheme allowing for this. Therefore, the extension of a PPF account must be done by the account holder themselves.

if the PPF account is continued after maturity for a further block period of 5 years, the subscriber is eligible to make partial withdrawals not exceeding one every year subject to the condition that the total of the withdrawals, during the 5 year block period, shall not exceed 60 per cent of the balance at his credit at the commencement of the said period. Generated Answer
----------------
After extending a Public Provident Fund (PPF) account for a further block period of 5 years, you are eligible to make partial withdrawals subject to certain conditions. Specifically:

1. You can make one withdrawal every financial year.
2. The total amount you can withdraw during the 5-year block period cannot exceed 60% of the balance available at the beginning of the block period. 
3. Withdrawals can be made either in one installment in a single financial year or in multiple installments across different years as per your requirements.

It is important to keep track of the total withdrawals to ensure that the limit of 60% is not exceeded during the block period.

is there tax concessions in the extended period also (Public Provident Fund Account Extension Form-)

Expected Answer
---------------
The interest credited to the fund including interest allowed during the extended period and withdrawal from the fund is exempt from income tax

Generated Answer
----------------
Yes, tax concessions under Section 80-C of the Income Tax Act apply to contributions made to a Public Provident Fund (PPF) account during the extended period as long as the subscriber makes the contributions from their taxable income. This means that contributions made during the continued blocks of five years after the initial maturity period would qualify for tax relief, subject to the annual limit specified under the law. However, it is important to ensure that the contributions made during the extension must be eligible as per the provisions in place at that time.

Attachment of credit balance in Public Provident Fund Account under orders of Income Tax authorities in respect of any debt or liability incurred by the subscriber:- It has been clarified by the CBDT and the Ministry of Law that Section 9 of the Public Provident fund Act applies only to attachment under a decree/order of a Court of Law and not to attachment by the Income Tax Authorities. Tax-deduction under Section 80-C of Income Tax Act on deposits made after 15 years in PPF account without exercising option for continuance of account:- (1) I am directed to say that paragraph 9(3A) of PPF Scheme, 1968 provides for continuance of account on the expiry of 15 years for a block period of 5 years and so on, if the subscriber exercises an option within one year after the expiry of 15 years. (2) A question arose as to whether the deposits made after 15 years without exercising the option for continuance of the account would enjoy concession under Section 80-C of Income Tax Act. The matter was taken up with the Department of Revenue (Central Board of Direct Taxes). The CBDT has clarified that the benefits of Section 80-C of Income Tax Act will not be available on deposits made in PPF account after expiry of 15 years without exercising option for continuance of the account. (iv) The interest credited in the PPF account is not treated as reinvestment for the purpose of Section 80-C of Income Tax Act as it is totally tax free and does not form part of the taxable income. (v) The balance held in the PPF account is completely free from Wealth Tax. The condition that the assets must be held for a period of at least six months before valuation date, does not apply to the P.P. Fund. (vi) The contribution paid into the fund in repayment of loans will not be eligible for rebate under Section 80-C of the Income Tax Act. (2) Freedom form court attachment: The balance to the credit of a subscriber in his account is not subject to attachment under any order or decree of a court in respect of any debt or other liability incurred by him. (3) Attachment of credit balance in PPF Account by Income Tax and Estate Duty Authorities:- Section 9 of the Public Provident Fund Act gives freedom only from attachment under a decree/order of a court of law and not to attachment by the Income Tax and Estate Duty Authorities. In view of this, the amount standing to the credit of subscriber in his PPF account shall be liable to attachment under any order of the Income Tax and Estate Duty Authorities in respect of any debt or liability incurred by the subscriber. 12. What withdrawals can I make in the extended perios (Public Provident Fund Account Extension Form-)

Expected Answer
---------------
During the extended period of 5 years, a subscriber is eligible to make partial withdrawal not exceeding one in every financial year subject to the condition that total withdrawal during the 5 years shall not exceed 60% of the balance to his credit at the commencement of the period.

Generated Answer
----------------
During the extended period of a Public Provident Fund (PPF) account, you are allowed to make partial withdrawals, subject to certain conditions. Specifically, you can make one withdrawal in each financial year, and the total withdrawals during the entire 5-year block period shall not exceed 60% of the balance to your credit at the commencement of that block period. You can choose to make the withdrawal as a single amount or in yearly installments.

Public Provident Fund Scheme, 1968—Non –adherence of instructions:- (1) The Reserve Bank of India vide their letter No. CO.DT.15.02.001/4544/99-2000 dated 21st February 2000 has informed that branches dealing with Public Provident Fund Scheme are not properly adhering to the instructions relating to the operation of the Scheme. (2) To ensure that the above mentioned discrepancies do not occur, we briefly enumerate the guidelines on these points in this regard. (A) Withdrawal from the fund:- (i) Anytime after the expiry of 5 years from the end of the financial year in which the initial subscription was made, the subscriber may withdraw 50% of the balance to his credit at the end of 4th year immediately preceding the year of withdrawal or the amount at the end of the preceding year whichever is lower. Question
--------
what details need to be given for extension of the ppf account (Public Provident Fund Account Extension Form-)

Expected Answer
---------------
Your name , PPF account number , date of the PPF accoutn maturing and address

Generated Answer
----------------
To extend a Public Provident Fund (PPF) account, the account holder needs to submit Form-4 within one year from the date of maturity of the account. The details required in Form-4 typically include:

1. **Account Holder's Information**: Name, address, and contact details of the account holder.
  
2. **Account Number**: The specific PPF account number for which the extension is being requested.

3. **Declaration**: A declaration stating that the customer is not a Non-Resident Indian (NRI) at the time of maturity.

4. **Extension Option**: The choice about whether to extend the account with regular deposits or to continue without further deposits.

5. **Signature/Thumb Impression**: The account holder's signature or thumb impression for verification.

6. **Additional Documents**: Any other supporting documents as required by the bank, which may include identification proof and address proof as per KYC norms.

It is advisable to check with the specific bank for any additional requirements or forms that may need to be completed for the extension process.

Expected Answer
---------------
The maximum limit equivalent to two months' net take-home salary is a completely new, separate credit line allocated specifically for this emergency facility. It does not overwrite, consume, or combine with any existing loan limits or standard overdraft arrangements you might already have running with the bank. It operates independently as a temporary pocket of emergency cash tied directly to the steady, verified monthly salary income deposited into your designated savings account.

----------------
The equivalent to two months' net salary refers to the total new limit allowed for the overdraft facility. This means that the new overdraft limit can be up to two times your net monthly salary in addition to any existing limit. QUESTION 190
======================================================================

Question
--------
what does ""reducing drawing power basis"" mean (overdraft against salary form)

Expected Answer
---------------
Operating on a reducing drawing power basis means your maximum borrowing limit automatically shrinks in equal parts every month as you pay it back, rather than acting like a reusable credit card. For example, if you take a ₹60,000 overdraft for a 6-month timeline, your spending cap starts at ₹60,000. When Month 1 ends and you make your first repayment installment, the bank permanently lowers your spending boundary by ₹10,000 down to ₹50,000. Even if you clear the balance early, you cannot pull that money back out; the overall limit continues to drop month-by-month until your debt hits zero.

Generated Answer
----------------
"Reducing drawing power basis" in the context of an overdraft facility means that the amount that a borrower can withdraw or utilize from their overdraft account decreases over time as they pay off the principal balance. Essentially, the facility allows the borrower to withdraw funds up to a certain limit at the beginning, which is based on their creditworthiness and account type, but as they make repayments toward the principal amount, their available limit reduces correspondingly. 

For example, if a borrower has an overdraft limit of ₹10 lakhs and they have drawn ₹5 lakhs, the drawing power may still allow them to withdraw the remaining amount. However, as they repay portions of that ₹5 lakhs, their available drawing power decreases by the amount they repay. 

This structure is particularly common in home loan overdrafts, like SBI Maxgain, where the borrower pays EMIs while simultaneously reducing their drawing limit over time, reflecting the diminishing debt as they make regular repayments.

QUESTION 191

Question
--------
what is MCLR (overdraft against salary form)

Expected Answer
---------------
MCLR stands for Marginal Cost of Funds Based Lending Rate. It is the internal benchmark floor interest rate below which a bank is legally not allowed to lend money to any customer. This rate is calculated automatically by the bank based on how much it costs them to maintain funds and pay interest on customer deposits. Because this overdraft uses a ""6 months MCLR,"" your interest rate is tied to this baseline and will be reviewed and updated by the bank every six months to match prevailing economic market conditions.

Generated Answer
----------------
MCLR stands for Marginal Cost of Funds Based Lending Rate. It is the minimum interest rate that a bank can set on its loans, and it is determined based on the bank's cost of funds, which includes various factors such as interest rates on savings, borrowing rates, and operational costs. 

In the context of an overdraft against salary, the MCLR would be used to determine the interest rate charged on the overdraft facility. The rates are typically linked to a specific tenor of the MCLR (e.g., 1-year MCLR or 2-year MCLR) and are added to a spread or margin set by the bank. 

For instance, in the case of the SBI, if the MCLR is 8.70%, and the overdraft interest rate is 1.45% above the MCLR for a certain loan amount, the effective interest rate on the overdraft would be 10.15%.

Question
--------
what is bps (overdraft against salary form)

Expected Answer
---------------
bps stands for Basis Points, which is a standard financial unit of measurement used by banks to describe minor changes or markups in interest rates. One single basis point is equal to exactly 0.01% (one-hundredth of a percentage point). In the context of this form, when the bank charges a rate ""above the MCLR,"" they use bps as a clear, precise way to state their added profit margin without causing rounding confusion. For example, if the bank decides to charge you a premium margin of ""250 bps"" over a baseline MCLR of 8.50%, your total effective interest rate will be exactly 11.00%.

Generated Answer
----------------
In the context of banking, "bps" typically stands for "basis points," which is a unit of measurement used to describe the percentage change in interest rates or other financial percentages. It is calculated as one one-hundredth of a percentage point (0.01%). However, the specific term "bps (overdraft against salary form)" appears to be referring to a particular overdraft facility that may use basis points to indicate the interest rate spread or fees associated with that overdraft facility in relation to a salary package.

If you are looking for specific details about the "overdraft against salary form," it would generally refer to the documentation or process required for customers who wish to avail themselves of an overdraft facility linked to their salary account. This typically involves providing certain documentation, which may include proof of employment, salary statements, identification, and completion of the bank's application form for the overdraft facility.

QUESTION 193

Question
--------
what if latest 2 months salary slips cannot be produced (overdraft against salary form)

Expected Answer
---------------
If you cannot provide your latest two months' consecutive salary slips, the bank will reject your overdraft application instantly.

Generated Answer
----------------
If you cannot produce the latest 2 months' salary slips when applying for an overdraft against your salary form, you may need to explore alternative methods to verify your income. Here are a few options you could consider:

1. **Use Previous Salary Slips**: If you have salary slips from previous months that reflect a consistent income, you can try submitting those as part of your application, along with an explanation for why the latest slips are unavailable.

2. **Bank Statements**: You could provide bank statements that show the direct deposits of your salary over the previous few months. This can serve as supplementary proof of income.

3. **Letter from Employer**: Request your employer to provide a letter confirming your employment status and salary. This letter may need to be on official letterhead and include signatures as verification.

4. **Form 16/ITR**: If you have filed your income tax returns or have a Form 16 issued by your employer, you may submit these as proof of income, especially if they cover the relevant time frame.

5. **Contact the Bank**: Reach out to your bank's customer service for guidance. They may have specific allowances or alternative documentation you can provide in lieu of the salary slips.

Ultimately, the bank will evaluate your application based on the documents you can provide and your overall financial profile, so maintaining open communication with them is key.

chemical alterations. 5.3 Monitoring Operations in all Accounts 5.3.1 A system of close monitoring of cash withdrawal for large amounts should be put in place. Where third party cheques, drafts, etc. are deposited in the existing and newly opened accounts followed by cash withdrawals for large amounts, the banks should keep a proper vigil over the requests of their clients for such cash withdrawals for large amounts. 5.3.2 The banks should introduce a system of closely monitoring cash deposits and withdrawals for Rs. 5 lakh and above not only in deposit accounts but also in all other accounts like cash credit/overdraft etc. The banks/branches should also maintain a separate register to record details of individual cash deposits and withdrawals for Rs. 5 lakh and above. The details recorded should include, in the case of deposits, the name of the account holder, account number, amount deposited and in the case of withdrawals, the name of the account holder, account number, amount of withdrawal and name of the beneficiary of the cheque. Further, any cash deposits or withdrawals of Rs. 5 lakh and above should be reported by the Branch Manager to the Head Office on a fortnightly basis along with full particulars, such as name of the account holder, account number, date of opening the account, etc. On receipt of these statements from branches, the Head Office should immediately scrutinise the details thereof and have the transactions looked into by deputing officials, if the transactions prima facie appear to be dubious or giving rise to suspicion. The inspecting officials 15 from the Reserve Bank during the course of their inspections will also be looking into the statements submitted by the branches. 5.3.3 The other important areas in the payment of cheques wherein due caution need to be exercised are verification of drawer's signature, custody of specimen signature cards, supervision over issue of cheque books and control over custody of blank cheque books/leaves. While need for examining cheques for large amounts under Ultra Violet Ray Lamps is recognised by all banks, in practice it is rarely done as there is often a tendency to be lax in the matter resulting in avoidable loss. In addition, due care should be exercised in regard to issue and custody of tokens, movement of cheques tendered across the counter and custody of all instruments after they are paid by the banks. Depositors/ Customers should be asked to surrender unused cheque books before closing/transferring the accounts. Also safe custody of specimen signature cards is of utmost importance, especially when operating instructions are changed, the change should be duly verified by a senior official in the branch. 5.4 5.5 Issue of Cheque Books Fresh cheque books should be issued only against production of duly signed requisition slips from previous cheque book issued to the party. QUESTION 194

Question
--------
what is ULB (PM SVANidhi form)

Expected Answer
---------------
Based on the PM SVANidhi Loan Application Form and official guidelines, a ULB stands for Urban Local Body (such as your local Municipal Corporation, Municipal Council, or Town Vending Committee). The ULB details, such as a Vendor ID Card, a Certificate of Vending, or a Letter of Recommendation (LoR) number issued electronically by the municipality, are mandatory requirements because they act as the official government ""Proof of Vending"". Since this loan requires zero physical security or collateral, the ULB data is required by the bank to verify that you are a genuine micro-entrepreneur legally operating within the city's jurisdiction.

Generated Answer
----------------
In the context of the PM SVANidhi loan application form, ULB stands for Urban Local Body. ULBs are administrative bodies that govern cities and towns in India. They are responsible for local governance and providing various services to the citizens within their jurisdictions. For the PM SVANidhi scheme, the ULBs play a crucial role in issuing the Certificate of Vending (CoV) or Letter of Recommendation (LoR) for street vendors, which are necessary for them to apply for the loan.

Question
--------
important pointers while filling (PM SVANidhi form)

Expected Answer
---------------
First, ensure you have a valid, active mobile number linked to your Aadhaar Card, as the form relies heavily on e-KYC verification. Second, you must select your correct type of vending framework—whether you are a Stationary Vendor (having a fixed stall at a specific landmark) or a Mobile Vendor (moving from place to place). Third, if you do not possess a formal pre-issued Vendor ID card, you must actively request a white-paper inquiry from your local town committee to generate an official Letter of Recommendation (LoR) number on the PM SVANidhi portal before submitting your application to the bank, as leaving the Proof of Vending row blank will result in immediate system rejection.

----------------
When filling out the PM SVANidhi application form, it is essential to pay attention to the following important pointers:

1. **Correct Language**: Ensure that you are using the correct language version of the application form that you are comfortable with (e.g., English, Hindi, Tamil, etc.).

2. **Accurate Information**: Fill in all personal details accurately, including name, address, contact information, and other identifying details. Double-check spellings and numerals.

3. **Eligibility Criteria**: Review and confirm that you meet the eligibility requirements for the PM SVANidhi scheme before submission.

4. **Documentation**: Attach all necessary documents as specified in the application form. This may include identity proof, address proof, and any other required supporting documents.

5. **Signature**: Ensure you sign the application form where requested. A missing signature could result in application rejection.

6. **Date Format**: Use the correct date format (DD/MM/YYYY) consistently throughout the form, particularly in sections requiring dates.

7. **Clear and Legible Handwriting**: If completing the form by hand, ensure that your handwriting is clear and legible. Avoid any corrections or overwrites that could lead to confusion.

8. **Review Before Submission**: Before finalizing your application, review the entire form to ensure all information is complete and accurate.

9. **Contact Details**: Provide a reliable phone number and email address for further communication or verification.

10. **Submission Procedure**: Follow the specified procedure for submitting the application, whether in-person, online, or via postal services, as mentioned in the guidelines of the scheme.

By keeping these pointers in mind, you can help ensure a smooth application process for the PM SVANidhi scheme.

114H(3)(c). 5.5.2 For high value accounts, there is a three-stage due diligence procedure- electronic stage, paper search and relationship manager enquiry. First, RFI needs to search its electronic searchable database in case of a customer. If this includes following information, no further paper record search by RFI is required:  the account holder’s residence status for tax purposes;  the account holder’s residence address and mailing address currently on file with the reporting financial institution;  the account holder’s telephone number or numbers currently on file, if any, with the reporting financial institution; 30 | P a g e  in the case of financial accounts other than depository accounts, whether there are standing instructions (other than a Depository Account in the case of CRS) to transfer funds in the account to another account (including an account at another branch of the reporting financial institution or another financial institution);  whether there is a current “in-care-of” address or “hold mail” instruction for the account holder; and  whether there is any power of attorney or signatory authority for the account. Figure: Due Diligence for Preexisting, High Value, Individual Accounts 5.5.3 If the electronic searchable database includes fields for and capture all of the above information, then Reporting Financial Institution is not required to do a paper record search. 5.5.4 But if it does not, then RFI needs to review the current customer master file for paper search and the documents obtained during the last five years for identification of any of the following indicia: 31 | P a g e  The most recent documentary evidence;  The most recent account opening contract or documentation;  The most recent documentation obtained by the Reporting FI pursuant to rules framed under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 (15 of 2003) or any other law for the time being in force;  Any power of attorney or signature authority forms currently in effect; and  Any standing instructions (other than a Depository Account in the case of CRS) to transfer fund currently in effect. Relationship Manager (RM) Test 5.5.5 In addition to above electronic and paper search, RFI has to apply Relationship Manager (RM) test on the high value accounts. A relationship manager is an employee or officer of the financial institution who has been assigned responsibility for specific Account Holders on an ongoing basis. A relationship manager will provide advice to Account Holders regarding their accounts as well as recommending and arranging for the provision of financial products, services and other related assistance. Relationship management must be more than ancillary or incidental to a person’s job role. Thus a person with some contact with Account Holders, but whose functions are administrative or clerical nature, is not considered to be a relationship manager. RFI must consider whether any relationship manager associated with an account, which includes any accounts aggregated with such an account, has actual knowledge that would identify the Account Holder as a Reportable Person. The relationship manager also has an important role in identifying any change of circumstance in relation to

QUESTION 199

Question
--------
what are processing fees

Expected Answer
---------------
valuation fees and legal fees (loan against property allocation form)","This is the fee the bank charges to cover the administrative work of reviewing your loan application. This fee goes directly to that external engineer for their technical assessment of your property value. This fee goes directly to that external lawyer for their title-search assessment of your property such as whether the property is caught in a family inheritance dispute, has an active court case against it, or was already secretly mortgaged to another bank..

Generated Answer
----------------
Processing fees are charges levied by a bank or financial institution for the processing of a loan or credit application. These fees are intended to cover the administrative costs related to evaluating and approving the loan. The amount of processing fees can vary depending on the type of loan, the loan amount, and the specific terms and conditions set by the bank.

For example, in the context provided:

- Personal loans can have processing fees that range from a percentage of the loan amount (like 1% for certain loans) to a fixed amount (such as a minimum of Rs 1,000).
- For specific types of loans, such as auto loans, fees can vary based on the loan amount (for instance, ₹750 for loans up to ₹5 Lakhs, and increasing with the loan amount).
- Other loans, like loans against property or securities, may have fixed processing fees or a percentage based on the loan amount.

It's important to note that these fees often do not include additional charges such as GST or other legal and governmental fees that may apply.

QUESTION 201

Question
--------
what is LTV and how much is allowed (loan against property allocation form)

Expected Answer
---------------
If the independent evaluator prices your home at ₹1 Crore, the bank will only give you a loan of roughly ₹50 Lakhs to ₹65 Lakhs to protect themselves from market drops. Tendering an unrealistically high request will slow down your approval. For a standard Personal Loan Against Property (P-LAP), SBI's internal guidelines actually cap the LTV ratio—at 65% for loan amounts up to ₹1 Crore, and 60% for loans above ₹1 Crore.

Generated Answer
----------------
The Loan-to-Value (LTV) ratio is a financial term used to express the ratio of a loan to the value of an asset purchased. Specifically, it is the amount of the loan divided by the appraised value of the property being financed. A higher LTV ratio indicates higher risk for the lender, as it signifies that a larger portion of the property's value is being borrowed.

For loan against property, the LTV allowed is typically up to 75% of the property value. This means that you can obtain a loan amount that is 75% of the appraised value of the property you are using as collateral.

QUESTION 202
======================================================================

Question
--------
difference in bullet repayment and emi schemes (gold loan application form)

Expected Answer
---------------
Under the Bullet Repayment scheme, a borrower does not pay any periodic installments to the bank during the tenure of the loan. Instead, the entire principal loan amount, along with all accumulated interest, is paid back in one single lump sum (the ""bullet"") at the end of the loan period (e.g., at 3, 6, or 12 months). Conversely, under an EMI-Based scheme, the loan is paid off steadily over a fixed schedule through monthly installments comprising both a portion of the principal amount and the accrued interest, which progressively reduces the total outstanding debt balance until the end of the tenure.

Generated Answer
----------------
The main differences between the bullet repayment and EMI schemes for SBI gold loans are as follows:

1. **Repayment Structure**:
   - **Bullet Repayment**: In this scheme, the borrower repays the entire principal and interest amount in a lump sum at the end of the loan tenure (which can be 3 months, 6 months, or 12 months). There are no monthly payments during the term.
   - **EMI Scheme**: In this scheme, the borrower repays the loan through monthly Equated Monthly Installments (EMIs) that include both principal and interest. The repayment starts from the month following the disbursement of the loan.

2. **Loan Tenure**:
   - **Bullet Repayment**: This option is typically offered for shorter terms, specifically 3 months, 6 months, or 12 months.
   - **EMI Scheme**: The maximum repayment period for an EMI-based gold loan is up to 36 months.

3. **Payment Frequency**:
   - **Bullet Repayment**: The borrower makes a single payment at the end of the tenure, making it suitable for those who expect to have a lump sum available at that time.
   - **EMI Scheme**: Payments are made monthly, which may be easier for borrowers who want to manage their cash flow over time by paying smaller amounts regularly.

4. **Interest Calculation**:
   - **Bullet Repayment**: Interest is typically calculated for the entire loan tenure and paid at once at the end.
   - **EMI Scheme**: Interest is calculated and applied to each monthly installment, allowing borrowers to reduce the principal with each payment.

In summary, the choice between bullet repayment and EMI schemes mainly depends on the borrower’s financial situation and ability to make payments either at the end of the loan period or on a monthly basis.

Question
--------
what is realty gold loan and why does it require builder letters (gold loan application form)

Expected Answer
---------------
An SBI Realty Gold Loan is a specialized variant designed exclusively for existing SBI Home Loan borrowers to fulfill funding shortfalls or to pay for unexpected property cost increases, stamp duties, and registration charges. The application form mandates the submission of a ""Letter from the Builder"" (in the case of flat purchases) along with a home loan arrangement letter to ensure that the gold loan proceeds are legally mapped and verified strictly against an active, authorized real estate project transaction rather than being diverted toward speculative or unauthorized uses.

Generated Answer
----------------
A Realty Gold Loan is a specific type of gold loan offered by banks like the State Bank of India (SBI) that enables individuals to borrow money by pledging their gold assets, such as gold jewelry or coins, while using the proceeds to finance real estate projects or investments. This loan can often be utilized for purposes like purchasing property, funding construction or renovation, or catering to other real estate-related expenses.

The requirement for builder letters in the gold loan application process may be linked to several reasons:

1. **Verification of Property Details**: Builder letters can confirm the legitimacy and authenticity of any property-related transactions the borrower is involved in, ensuring that the bank has rid the risk of fraudulent activities linked to property investments.

2. **Loan Purpose Specification**: Such letters provide clarity on how the loan amount will be utilized, which can be critical for the bank to assess the loan application. They can outline the terms of property purchase, construction timelines, or other pertinent details.

3. **Loan Amount Calculation**: The value indicated in the builder letter helps the bank in determining the appropriate loan amount against the gold pledged, considering it is tied to real estate which usually has specific financing requirements.

In summary, a Realty Gold Loan is a financial product that uses gold as collateral for securing funds that can be applied towards real estate investments, and builder letters are integral for verifying property-related details, ensuring transparency, and guiding the loan process.

QUESTION 204

Question
--------
what is gross weight and net weight and how to enter it (gold loan application form)

Expected Answer
---------------
In the application's ornaments table, Gross Weight refers to the total weight of the jewelry when placed on the scale as a whole, whereas Net Weight represents the exact weight of pure, actual gold after subtracting the weight of any non-precious stones, diamonds, beads, or internal structural wax (lac). As a customer, you must leave this entire section completely blank on your application. The bank will call an independent, authorized Gold Appraiser to test and physically weigh your jewelry at the branch, and they will be the ones to calculate, enter, and formally sign off on these metrics.

Generated Answer
----------------
In the context of a gold loan application, gross weight and net weight refer to different measurements of the gold being pledged as collateral.

1. **Gross Weight**: This is the total weight of the gold item(s) including any additional elements such as chains, clasps, or unnecessary components that are part of the gold ornaments. It essentially measures the entire weight of the gold items without any deductions.

2. **Net Weight**: This is the weight of the gold content itself, excluding any additional materials or components that do not contribute to the gold's monetary value. In a gold loan application, the net weight is important as it is what will be considered for assessing the loan amount that can be granted based on gold purity and value.

When filling out the gold loan application form, you should enter the gross weight of the gold items—including all decorations and attachments—and the net weight—representing only the gold portion. It’s crucial to ensure that the measurements are accurate as they impact the terms of the gold loan, including the amount of money you may receive as a loan.

QUESTION 205

Question
--------
what is 75% LTV (gold loan application form)

Expected Answer
---------------
LTV stands for Loan-to-Value, and a 75% LTV ratio means that the bank is legally capped from extending a credit amount that exceeds 75% of the appraised market value of your pure gold asset. According to the guidelines, the borrower is contractually bound to maintain this 75% baseline throughout the loan tenure. If international gold market prices crash heavily while your loan is active, causing your outstanding debt to breach the 75% margin of your pledged asset's new value, the bank reserves the right to issue an immediate margin call for you to pay down cash or deposit extra ornaments to restore the ratio.

Generated Answer
----------------
The Loan to Value (LTV) ratio of up to 75% in the context of a gold loan application means that the bank will provide a loan amount that is up to 75% of the market value of the gold being pledged as collateral. For example, if the market value of the gold collateral is ₹1,00,000, the maximum loan amount that can be availed would be ₹75,000. This ensures that the bank is covered in case of default, while allowing borrowers to access a significant portion of their gold's value.
